source.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ מִקְטַ֣ר קְטֹ֑רֶת עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make an altar, a place of burning of incense; [of] wood of acacia you will make it.

en.L: And you will make an altar [for] burning incense; [of] acacia wood you will make it.
en.B: You are to make an altar for burning incense, and you are to make it from acacia wood.
en.R: Build an altar for burning incense. Make it out of acacia wood.

decisions.choice: an altar, a place for burning incense: the altar of incense
decisions.reason: The phrase names what the altar is for: incense is turned to smoke on it. It is the gold altar that stood inside the tent, distinct from the bronze altar of burnt offering in the courtyard (27:1-8; 40:5-6, 26-27).

decisions.choice: the instructions for the tent continue
decisions.reason: God's words to Moses that began in 25:1 go on here without a break. The altar of incense is described after the priests' ordination (chapter 29), not with the other furnishings of the holy place in chapters 25-27; verses 7-10 show why: its use belongs to Aaron's regular service.

decisions.choice: [for] ... [of]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs to join the Hebrew phrases.

source.text: אַמָּ֨ה אָרְכּ֜וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה רָחְבּוֹ֙ רָב֣וּעַ יִהְיֶ֔ה וְאַמָּתַ֖יִם קֹמָת֑וֹ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ קַרְנֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: A cubit its length and a cubit its breadth, square it will be, and two cubits its height; from it its horns.

en.L: A cubit its length and a cubit its width; square it will be, and two cubits its height; its horns [will be] from it.
en.B: Make it square, {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} on each side and {{units:about 3 feet|two cubits}} high, with its horns of one piece with it.
en.R: It should be square, {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} on each side and {{units:about 3 feet|two cubits}} tall. The horns on its corners must be part of the altar itself.

decisions.choice: cubit: a measure of length, about a foot and a half
decisions.reason: The cubit was the length of a forearm, from elbow to fingertip, roughly 18 inches. So the altar was about a foot and a half square and about three feet high.

decisions.choice: its horns from it: horn-shaped corners made of one piece with the altar
decisions.reason: Altars had horn-like points rising from their four corners, as the bronze altar did (27:2). They were made with the altar, not fixed on afterward. The horns were the most holy part of an altar: blood was put on them (verse 10; 29:12), and a person seeking protection took hold of them (1 Kings 1:50).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}}; {{units:about 3 feet|two cubits}}
decisions.reason: Units setting: a modern measure by default, the cubit as the alternative. Literal keeps "cubit".

decisions.choice: on its corners
decisions.reason: Readable says where the horns were, as 27:2 does for the bronze altar.

source.text: וְצִפִּיתָ֨ אֹת֜וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֗וֹר אֶת־גַּגּ֧וֹ וְאֶת־קִירֹתָ֛יו סָבִ֖יב וְאֶת־קַרְנֹתָ֑יו וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will overlay it [with] pure gold, its top and its sides all around and its horns; and you will make for it a molding of gold all around.

en.L: And you will overlay it [with] pure gold, its top and its sides all around and its horns; and you will make for it a molding of gold all around.
en.B: Overlay it with pure gold: the top, the sides all the way around, and the horns. Then run a gold molding around it.
en.R: Cover the whole altar with pure gold: the top, all four sides, and the horns. Put a gold edging all the way around it.

decisions.choice: overlay with pure gold: cover the wood with plates of gold
decisions.reason: The acacia wood was covered with gold, as the ark and the table were (25:11, 24). Because of its gold it is called "the gold altar" (39:38; 40:5).

decisions.choice: a molding: a raised border or rim
decisions.reason: The word means a border running around the top, like the one on the ark and the table (25:11, 24). Its exact shape is not described.

decisions.choice: its sides: literally "its walls"
decisions.reason: The word means the walls or sides of the box-shaped altar.

decisions.choice: gold edging
decisions.reason: Readable says "edging" for the less familiar "molding".

source.text: וּשְׁתֵּי֩ טַבְּעֹ֨ת זָהָ֜ב תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ׀מִתַּ֣חַת לְזֵר֗וֹ עַ֚ל שְׁתֵּ֣י צַלְעֹתָ֔יו תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַל־שְׁנֵ֣י צִדָּ֑יו וְהָיָה֙ לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֥את אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֵֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And two rings of gold you will make for it under its molding; on its two ribs you will make [them], on its two sides; and they will become holders for poles to carry it by them.

en.L: And two rings of gold you will make for it, under its molding; on its two ribs you will make [them], on its two sides. And they will be holders for poles, to carry it with them.
en.B: Make two gold rings for it below the molding, on its two opposite sides, to hold the poles that it is carried with.
en.R: Make two gold rings and attach them below the edging, on opposite sides of the altar. These rings will hold the poles used to carry it.

decisions.choice: two rings ... on its two sides: one ring on each of two opposite sides
alternatives: two rings on each side, four in all
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "two rings" and then "on its two sides". It may mean two rings in all, one on each side, or two rings on each side, four in all, as the ark had (25:12). The parallel account in 37:27 has the same wording.

decisions.choice: its ribs: its sides, perhaps its corners
decisions.reason: The word means a rib or side. Set beside "its two sides", it likely repeats the thought; some take it as the corners.

decisions.choice: holders for poles to carry it: the altar was portable
decisions.reason: Like the ark and the table, the altar was carried on poles through the rings, so that no one touched it as Israel moved through the wilderness (25:14, 27; Numbers 4:11).

decisions.choice: two opposite sides
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two phrases "on its two ribs" and "on its two sides" into one.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַבַּדִּ֖ים עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make the poles [of] wood of acacia, and you will overlay them [with] gold.

en.L: And you will make the poles [of] acacia wood, and you will overlay them [with] gold.
en.B: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
en.R: Make the poles out of acacia wood and cover them with gold.

decisions.choice: the poles: made like those of the ark and the table
decisions.reason: The same instruction is given for the poles of the ark and the table (25:13, 28).

source.text: וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אֹתוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־אֲרֹ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֑ת לִפְנֵ֣י הַכַּפֹּ֗רֶת אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־הָ֣עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִוָּעֵ֥ד לְךָ֖ שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put it before the curtain which [is] over the ark of the testimony, before the atonement cover which [is] over the testimony, where I will meet with you there.

en.L: And you will put it before the veil that [is] by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat that [is] over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
en.B: Set it in front of the curtain that hangs before the ark of the testimony, in front of the mercy seat that covers the testimony, where I will meet with you.
en.R: Put the altar in front of the curtain that hangs before the ark that holds the covenant tablets. It will face the lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered, which is over the tablets. That is where I will meet with you.

decisions.choice: the curtain: the veil that closed off the most holy place
decisions.reason: This is the inner curtain of 26:31-33, which separated the holy place from the most holy place where the ark stood. The altar of incense stood in the holy place, just outside it (40:26).

decisions.choice: the mercy seat: the lid of the ark, the place of atonement
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "make atonement". It names the gold lid of the ark (25:17-22), where blood was sprinkled on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:14-15). It may be rendered "atonement cover" or "place of atonement".

decisions.choice: the testimony: the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the two stone tablets of the covenant that were kept in the ark (25:16, 21; 31:18). "The ark of the testimony" is the ark that held them.

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets; the lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ark and its lid in plain words, as in chapter 25. Literal and Balanced keep "ark of the testimony" and "mercy seat".

decisions.choice: veil (Literal); curtain (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The inner curtain is the "veil" at Literal and the "curtain" at Balanced and Readable, as in chapter 26.

source.text: וְהִקְטִ֥יר עָלָ֛יו אַהֲרֹ֖ן קְטֹ֣רֶת סַמִּ֑ים בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֗קֶר בְּהֵיטִיב֛וֹ אֶת־הַנֵּרֹ֖ת יַקְטִירֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will make smoke on it Aaron incense of spices; in the morning, in the morning, when he tends the lamps, he will make it smoke.

en.L: And Aaron will burn on it incense of spices; morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he will burn it.
en.B: Each morning, as he sets the lamps in order, Aaron is to burn sweet-smelling incense on it.
en.R: Every morning, when Aaron takes care of the lamps, he must burn sweet-smelling incense on this altar.

decisions.choice: burn incense of spices: turn fragrant incense into smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke. The incense is made of the spices listed in verses 34-35.

decisions.choice: in the morning, in the morning: every morning
decisions.reason: The repeated phrase means morning after morning, each day.

decisions.choice: makes good the lamps: trims and refills them
decisions.reason: To "make the lamps good" means to clean, trim and refill the lamps of the lampstand that had burned through the night (27:20-21).

source.text: וּבְהַעֲלֹ֨ת אַהֲרֹ֧ן אֶת־הַנֵּרֹ֛ת בֵּ֥ין הָעֲרְבַּ֖יִם יַקְטִירֶ֑נָּה קְטֹ֧רֶת תָּמִ֛יד לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And when Aaron sets up the lamps between the evenings he will make it smoke, incense of continuity before Yahweh to your generations.

en.L: And when Aaron sets up the lamps between the evenings, he will burn it, a continual incense before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} throughout your generations.
en.B: And when he lights the lamps at dusk he is to burn it again. This is to be the regular incense offered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, generation after generation.
en.R: He must also burn it in the evening, when he lights the lamps. This incense must be burned before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every day, for all time to come.

decisions.choice: between the evenings: at dusk
decisions.reason: The phrase means the time between sunset and dark, as in 12:6 and 29:39, 41.

decisions.choice: sets up the lamps: lights them
decisions.reason: The verb means "make go up". Here it means lighting the lamps so that their flame rises, as in 25:37.

decisions.choice: continual: regular, offered every day without fail
decisions.reason: The word means something done regularly, not without a pause: incense was burned every morning and every evening, like the daily burnt offering (29:42).

decisions.choice: he ... again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "he" for the repeated "Aaron" and add "again" or "also" to show this is the second burning of the day.

source.text: לֹא־תַעֲל֥וּ עָלָ֛יו קְטֹ֥רֶת זָרָ֖ה וְעֹלָ֣ה וּמִנְחָ֑ה וְנֵ֕סֶךְ לֹ֥א תִסְּכ֖וּ עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must offer up on it incense strange, and a burnt offering and a grain offering, and a drink offering not you must pour out on it.

en.L: You must not offer up on it strange incense, or burnt offering, or grain offering; and drink offering you must not pour out on it.
en.B: Never burn unauthorized incense on it. It is not for burnt offerings or grain offerings, and no drink offering may be poured out on it.
en.R: Do not burn any other kind of incense on it. Do not offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, and do not pour drink offerings on it.

decisions.choice: strange incense: incense not made as God commanded
decisions.reason: "Strange" means foreign or not authorized. Here it is any incense other than the blend God prescribes in verses 34-38. The same word is used of the "strange fire" that Nadab and Abihu offered (Leviticus 10:1).

decisions.choice: burnt offering, grain offering, drink offering: offerings for the bronze altar
decisions.reason: These offerings belonged on the bronze altar in the courtyard (29:38-41). The gold altar was for incense alone.

decisions.choice: unauthorized (Balanced); any other kind of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "strange".

source.text: וְכִפֶּ֤ר אַהֲרֹן֙ עַל־קַרְנֹתָ֔יו אַחַ֖ת בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה מִדַּ֞ם חַטַּ֣את הַכִּפֻּרִ֗ים אַחַ֤ת בַּשָּׁנָה֙ יְכַפֵּ֤ר עָלָיו֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם קֹֽדֶשׁ־קָֽדָשִׁ֥ים ה֖וּא לַיהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And will make atonement Aaron on its horns once in the year; from the blood of the sin offering of the atonements once in the year he will make atonement on it, to your generations. Holiness of holinesses it [is] to Yahweh.

en.L: And Aaron will make atonement on its horns once in the year; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement once in the year he will make atonement on it throughout your generations. It [is] most holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Aaron is to make atonement on its horns one time each year, using blood from the sin offering of atonement. Once every year, generation after generation, atonement is to be made on it. It is most holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Once each year Aaron must put blood on the horns of this altar to make atonement for it. He must use blood from the sin offering that makes atonement. This must be done every year for all time to come. The altar is most holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: atonement on its horns once a year: on the Day of Atonement
decisions.reason: The once-yearly atonement with the blood of the sin offering points to the Day of Atonement, when the high priest put blood on the horns of the altar to cleanse it (Leviticus 16:18-19, 34; 23:27).

decisions.choice: make atonement on it: for the altar itself
alternatives: make atonement on it, for the people
decisions.reason: "On it" can mean on the altar or for the altar. Leviticus 16:18-19 shows the altar being cleansed and made holy from Israel's uncleanness, so the atonement is made for the altar.

decisions.choice: holiness of holinesses: most holy
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the word to make it as strong as it can be. The altar belongs wholly to the LORD (compare 29:37).

decisions.choice: put blood on the horns ... to make atonement for it
decisions.reason: Readable says how the atonement was made, by putting blood on the horns, following m2 and Leviticus 16:18.

decisions.choice: generation after generation (Balanced); for all time to come (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Throughout your generations" means for as long as Israel lasts.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech begins
decisions.reason: This is the first time since 25:1 that the narrator says God spoke to Moses. The rest of the chapter is four short speeches (verses 11, 17, 22, 34).

source.text: כִּ֣י תִשָּׂ֞א אֶת־רֹ֥אשׁ בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ללִפְקֻדֵיהֶם֒ וְנָ֨תְנ֜וּ אִ֣ישׁ כֹּ֧פֶר נַפְשׁ֛וֹ לַיהוָ֖ה בִּפְקֹ֣ד אֹתָ֑ם וְלֹא־יִהְיֶ֥ה בָהֶ֛ם נֶ֖גֶף בִּפְקֹ֥ד אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: When you lift up the head of the sons of Israel by their enrolled, then they will give each [man] a ransom of his life to Yahweh when enrolling them, and not will be among them a plague when enrolling them.

en.L: "When you lift up the head of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel according to those enrolled of them, then each [man] will give a ransom for his life to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when [you] enroll them, so that there will be no plague among them when [you] enroll them.
en.B: "Whenever you take a census of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and enroll them, every man is to give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a ransom for his life at his enrollment. That way no plague will fall on them while the count is being made.
en.R: "When you count the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, each man who is counted must pay {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a price to save his life. Then no deadly sickness will strike them while you are counting them.

decisions.choice: lift up the head: take a census, count
decisions.reason: To "lift up the head" of a people means to count them (Numbers 1:2, 49). The census in Numbers 1 counted the men of twenty years and older who could serve in the army (verse 14; Numbers 1:3).

decisions.choice: a ransom for his life: a payment that covers his life
decisions.reason: A ransom is the price paid to free or protect a life (21:30). Each man counted belongs to God, and the payment covers his life before God.

decisions.choice: no plague when you count them: a census was dangerous
decisions.reason: To count people was to claim them. When David counted Israel without such a ransom, a plague struck the people (2 Samuel 24:1-15). Here the payment guards against that.

decisions.choice: a price to save his life; deadly sickness
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ransom" and "plague" in plain words.

source.text: זֶ֣ה׀יִתְּנ֗וּ כָּל־הָעֹבֵר֙ עַל־הַפְּקֻדִ֔ים מַחֲצִ֥ית הַשֶּׁ֖קֶל בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֤ים גֵּרָה֙ הַשֶּׁ֔קֶל מַחֲצִ֣ית הַשֶּׁ֔קֶל תְּרוּמָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: This they will give, everyone who passes over to the enrolled: half of the shekel by the shekel of the holy place, twenty gerahs the shekel, half of the shekel a contribution to Yahweh.

en.L: This they will give, everyone who passes over to those enrolled: half of the shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary (twenty gerahs [is] the shekel), half of the shekel [as] a heave offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Each one who crosses over to join those already counted is to give this: {{units:about 1/5 ounce of silver|half a shekel}}, weighed by the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. This {{units:silver|half shekel}} is a contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Each man who is counted must give {{units:about 1/5 ounce of silver|half a shekel}}, weighed by the official sanctuary shekel. This silver is a gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: half a shekel: about a fifth of an ounce of silver
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight, not a coin; coins came much later. A shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce (11.5 grams), so half a shekel was about a fifth of an ounce of silver. A gerah was a twentieth of a shekel.

decisions.choice: the shekel of the sanctuary: the standard weight kept by the priests
decisions.reason: Weights differed from place to place. "The shekel of the sanctuary" was the standard, set at twenty gerahs, used for payments to God (Leviticus 27:25; Numbers 3:47).

decisions.choice: who passes over to those enrolled: who joins the counted
decisions.reason: The picture may be of each man crossing from the uncounted group to those already counted, or passing before the one counting. Either way it means each man who is counted.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 1/5 ounce of silver|half a shekel}}; {{units:silver|half shekel}}
decisions.reason: Units setting: the modern weight by default, the shekel as the alternative. "The shekel of the sanctuary" is the standard weight, so it stays in both. Literal keeps the shekel and gerahs.

decisions.choice: contribution (Balanced); gift (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means something lifted off and set apart for God. Literal says "heave offering".

source.text: כֹּ֗ל הָעֹבֵר֙ עַל־הַפְּקֻדִ֔ים מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה יִתֵּ֖ן תְּרוּמַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Everyone who passes over to the enrolled, from a son of twenty years and upward, will give the contribution of Yahweh.

en.L: Everyone who passes over to those enrolled, from a son of twenty years and upward, will give the heave offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: All who cross over to the counted, from twenty years old and up, are to give this contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Every man twenty years old or older who is counted must give this gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty years: twenty years old
decisions.reason: "A son of" so many years is the Hebrew way of giving a person's age. Twenty was the age at which men were counted for military service (Numbers 1:3).

decisions.choice: the contribution of Yahweh: the contribution given to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The phrase means the gift that belongs to the LORD, the half shekel of verse 13.

source.text: הֶֽעָשִׁ֣יר לֹֽא־יַרְבֶּ֗ה וְהַדַּל֙ לֹ֣א יַמְעִ֔יט מִֽמַּחֲצִ֖ית הַשָּׁ֑קֶל לָתֵת֙ אֶת־תְּרוּמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The rich not will make much, and the poor not will make little than half of the shekel, in giving the contribution of Yahweh to make atonement for your lives.

en.L: The rich [man] will not give more, and the poor [man] will not give less, than half of the shekel, when [you] give the heave offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to make atonement for your lives.
en.B: When you bring the contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to make atonement for your lives, the rich are not to give more than {{units:the 1/5 ounce|the half shekel}}, nor the poor less.
en.R: Rich people must not give more, and poor people must not give less. Everyone gives the same gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to make atonement for their lives.

decisions.choice: the rich no more, the poor no less: every life of the same worth to God
decisions.reason: Each man paid the same ransom, so no one could buy a better standing with God and no one was too poor to be counted. Every life counted alike.

decisions.choice: to make atonement for your lives: to cover your lives
decisions.reason: The payment covers each life before God, as the ransom of verse 12 does. "Lives" is literally "selves".

decisions.choice: {{units:the 1/5 ounce|the half shekel}}
decisions.reason: Units setting, as in verse 13. Readable leaves out the amount, which verse 13 has already given.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֞ אֶת־כֶּ֣סֶף הַכִּפֻּרִ֗ים מֵאֵת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְנָתַתָּ֣ אֹת֔וֹ עַל־עֲבֹדַ֖ת אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהָיָה֩ לִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל לְזִכָּרוֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And you will take the money of the atonements from the sons of Israel and give it for the service of the tent of meeting; and it will be for the sons of Israel a memorial before Yahweh, to make atonement for your lives.

en.L: And you will take the atonement money from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and give it for the service of the tent of meeting, and it will be for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel a memorial before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to make atonement for your lives."
en.B: Collect the atonement money from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and put it toward the work of the tent of meeting. It will be a reminder before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on behalf of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, making atonement for your lives."
en.R: Collect this money from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. It pays for atonement. Use it for the work of the tent of meeting. It will remind {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and it will make atonement for their lives."

decisions.choice: the atonement money: the silver paid as a ransom
decisions.reason: The silver is called by what it does: it makes atonement for the lives of those counted (verse 15).

decisions.choice: for the service of the tent of meeting: the silver was used in building it
decisions.reason: Exodus 38:25-28 tells that the silver from the census, a half shekel for each of 603,550 men, was used for the bases of the tabernacle and the hooks of its posts. Later the same tax supported the temple (2 Chronicles 24:6, 9).

decisions.choice: a memorial: a reminder
decisions.reason: The silver stands before the LORD as a reminder of the people for whom it was given, as the names on the high priest's stones do (28:12, 29).

decisions.choice: It pays for atonement
decisions.reason: Readable splits the phrase "atonement money" into its own short sentence.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: the second of four short speeches
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, a new set of instructions begins.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ כִּיּ֥וֹר נְחֹ֛שֶׁת וְכַנּ֥וֹ נְחֹ֖שֶׁת לְרָחְצָ֑ה וְנָתַתָּ֣ אֹת֗וֹ בֵּֽין־אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְנָתַתָּ֥ שָׁ֖מָּה מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make a basin of bronze and its stand of bronze for washing, and you will put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and you will put there water.

en.L: "And you will make a basin of bronze and its stand of bronze for washing; and you will put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and you will put water in it.
en.B: "Make a basin of bronze on a bronze stand, to be used for washing. Set it between the tent of meeting and the altar and fill it with water.
en.R: "Make a large bronze bowl with a bronze stand, for washing. Place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and fill it with water.

decisions.choice: basin: a large bowl for water
decisions.reason: The word means a basin or pot. Its size and shape are not given. Exodus 38:8 says it was made from the bronze mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

decisions.choice: its stand: the base it rested on
decisions.reason: The word means a base or pedestal.

decisions.choice: the altar: the bronze altar of burnt offering
decisions.reason: The basin stood in the courtyard, between the bronze altar and the entrance of the tent (40:7, 30).

decisions.choice: large bronze bowl
decisions.reason: Readable explains "basin".

source.text: וְרָחֲצ֛וּ אַהֲרֹ֥ן וּבָנָ֖יו מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־רַגְלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will wash Aaron and his sons from it their hands and their feet.

en.L: And Aaron and his sons will wash from it their hands and their feet.
en.B: From it Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and their feet.
en.R: Aaron and his sons must use water from it to wash their hands and their feet.

decisions.choice: wash hands and feet: the priests cleansed themselves before serving
decisions.reason: Priests went barefoot in the holy place and handled the offerings. Washing their hands and feet made them clean for that service (40:31-32).

decisions.choice: from it: with water drawn from the basin
decisions.reason: They washed with water taken from the basin, not by stepping into it.

source.text: בְּבֹאָ֞ם אֶל־אֹ֧הֶל מוֹעֵ֛ד יִרְחֲצוּ־מַ֖יִם וְלֹ֣א יָמֻ֑תוּ א֣וֹ בְגִשְׁתָּ֤ם אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לְשָׁרֵ֔ת לְהַקְטִ֥יר אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: When they go into the tent of meeting they will wash [with] water, and not they will die; or when they draw near to the altar to serve, to make smoke a fire offering to Yahweh,

en.L: When they go into the tent of meeting, they will wash [with] water, so that they will not die; or when they draw near to the altar to serve, to burn a fire offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: Each time they enter the tent of meeting, they must wash with water, so that they do not die. The same is true when they come near the altar to serve by burning an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:
en.R: Whenever they go into the tent of meeting, they must wash with water so that they do not die. And whenever they come to the altar to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by burning an offering,

decisions.choice: so that they do not die: God's holiness is dangerous to the unclean
decisions.reason: To come before God without the cleansing he commands is deadly (28:35, 43; Leviticus 10:1-2; 16:2).

decisions.choice: a fire offering: an offering burned by fire
decisions.reason: The word is linked to the word for "fire" and names offerings burned on the altar. Some connect it with a word for "gift" and render it "food offering".

decisions.choice: The same is true (Balanced); And whenever (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verse breaks off and its sentence is completed in verse 21. Balanced and Readable add words to bridge it.

source.text: וְרָחֲצ֛וּ יְדֵיהֶ֥ם וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָמֻ֑תוּ וְהָיְתָ֨ה לָהֶ֧ם חָק־עוֹלָ֛ם ל֥וֹ וּלְזַרְע֖וֹ לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: they will wash their hands and their feet, and not they will die; and it will be for them a statute of perpetuity, for him and for his offspring, to their generations.

en.L: they will wash their hands and their feet, so that they will not die. And it will be for them a statute forever, for him and for his offspring throughout their generations."
en.B: they must wash their hands and feet, so that they do not die. This is a statute for all time, for Aaron and his descendants, generation after generation."
en.R: they must wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. This is a rule for Aaron and his descendants for all time to come."

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a lasting rule
decisions.reason: The phrase means a rule that holds for as long as the priesthood lasts, as in 27:21 and 28:43.

decisions.choice: for him and his offspring: Aaron and the priests after him
decisions.reason: "Him" is Aaron; "his offspring" are his descendants, the priests of later generations.

decisions.choice: Aaron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Aaron for "him".

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: the third of four short speeches
decisions.reason: As in verses 11 and 17, a new set of instructions begins.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה קַח־לְךָ֮ בְּשָׂמִ֣ים רֹאשׁ֒ מָר־דְּרוֹר֙ חֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וְקִנְּמָן־בֶּ֥שֶׂם מַחֲצִית֖וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם וּקְנֵה־בֹ֖שֶׂם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמָאתָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, take for yourself spices, the best: myrrh of flowing five hundred, and cinnamon of spice half of it, two hundred fifty, and cane of spice two hundred fifty,

en.L: "And you, take for yourself the finest spices: flowing myrrh, 500 [shekels], and fragrant cinnamon, half as much, 250, and fragrant cane, 250,
en.B: "Take for yourself the choicest spices: {{units:about 12 1/2 pounds|500 shekels}} of free-flowing myrrh; half that amount, {{units:about 6 1/4 pounds|250 shekels}}, of sweet-smelling cinnamon; {{units:about 6 1/4 pounds|250 shekels}} of fragrant cane;
en.R: "Get the best spices: {{units:about 12 1/2 pounds|500 shekels}} of pure myrrh, {{units:about 6 1/4 pounds|250 shekels}} of sweet cinnamon, {{units:about 6 1/4 pounds|250 shekels}} of sweet-smelling cane,

decisions.choice: 500 ... 250: weights in shekels
decisions.reason: The unit is not named, but verse 24 shows these are shekels by the sanctuary standard. A shekel was about two-fifths of an ounce, so 500 shekels was about 12 1/2 pounds and 250 shekels about 6 1/4 pounds.

decisions.choice: flowing myrrh: myrrh in its purest form
decisions.reason: Myrrh is a fragrant resin from a shrub of Arabia and East Africa. "Flowing" may mean the resin that oozes out by itself, which was the finest, or myrrh that is liquid.

decisions.choice: cinnamon ... cane: fragrant spices, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: These spices cannot be identified with certainty. "Cinnamon" may be the bark of the cinnamon tree or a related plant. "Cane of spice" is a fragrant reed or grass, perhaps calamus or lemongrass (Isaiah 43:24; Jeremiah 6:20).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 12 1/2 pounds|500 shekels}}; {{units:about 6 1/4 pounds|250 shekels}}
decisions.reason: Units setting: modern weights by default, shekels as the alternative. Literal keeps the numbers and brackets "shekels".

decisions.choice: ("half as much" left out)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the weights and leaves out "half as much", which only repeats them.

source.text: וְקִדָּ֕ה חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְשֶׁ֥מֶן זַ֖יִת הִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: and cassia five hundred by the shekel of the holy place, and oil of olive a hin.

en.L: and cassia, 500, by the shekel of the sanctuary, and olive oil, a hin.
en.B: and {{units:about 12 1/2 pounds|500 shekels}} of cassia, all weighed by the shekel of the sanctuary; and {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of olive oil.
en.R: and {{units:about 12 1/2 pounds|500 shekels}} of cassia, weighed by the official sanctuary shekel. Also get {{units:about a gallon|a hin}} of olive oil.

decisions.choice: cassia: a fragrant bark, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: Cassia is most likely a bark related to cinnamon, but the plant cannot be identified with certainty.

decisions.choice: a hin: a liquid measure, about a gallon
decisions.reason: The hin was a measure for liquids such as oil and wine (29:40), roughly a gallon.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 12 1/2 pounds|500 shekels}}; {{units:about a gallon|a hin}}
decisions.reason: Units setting: modern measures by default, the shekel and hin as the alternative. The sanctuary shekel stays as the standard. Literal keeps "a hin".

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ אֹת֗וֹ שֶׁ֚מֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹ֔דֶשׁ רֹ֥קַח מִרְקַ֖חַת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֑חַ שֶׁ֥מֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make it an oil of anointing of holiness, an ointment of a mixture, [the] work of a perfumer; an oil of anointing of holiness it will be.

en.L: And you will make it [into] a holy anointing oil, a blended ointment, the work of a perfumer; a holy anointing oil it will be.
en.B: Out of these, prepare a holy oil for anointing, blended with a perfumer's skill. It is to be the holy anointing oil.
en.R: Mix them together the way a skilled perfume maker would, to make a holy oil for anointing. It will be the holy anointing oil.

decisions.choice: anointing oil of holiness: holy oil for anointing
decisions.reason: To anoint is to pour or smear oil on a person or thing, to set it apart for God's service (28:41; 29:7).

decisions.choice: an ointment of mixture, the work of a perfumer: a skillfully blended perfume
decisions.reason: The words come from a verb for mixing spices. The oil was to be prepared with the skill of a trained perfumer (37:29).

source.text: וּמָשַׁחְתָּ֥ ב֖וֹ אֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְאֵ֖ת אֲר֥וֹן הָעֵדֻֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will anoint with it the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,

en.L: And you will anoint with it the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
en.B: Use it to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony,
en.R: Use it to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark that holds the covenant tablets,

decisions.choice: you will anoint: the anointing is carried out in 40:9-11
decisions.reason: The tent and everything in it were anointed when the tabernacle was set up (40:9-11; Leviticus 8:10-11).

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ark, as in verse 6.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָן֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֶת־הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה וְאֶת־כֵּלֶ֑יהָ וְאֵ֖ת מִזְבַּ֥ח הַקְּטֹֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: and the table and all its articles, and the lampstand and its articles, and the altar of incense,

en.L: and the table and all its utensils, and the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
en.B: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
en.R: the table and all the things used with it, the lampstand and its tools, the altar for burning incense,

decisions.choice: articles: the utensils and tools that went with each piece
decisions.reason: The word covers any vessel or tool: the plates, dishes and pitchers of the table (25:29) and the snuffers and trays of the lampstand (25:38).

source.text: וְאֶת־מִזְבַּ֥ח הָעֹלָ֖ה וְאֶת־כָּל־כֵּלָ֑יו וְאֶת־הַכִּיֹּ֖ר וְאֶת־כַּנּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and the altar of the burnt offering and all its articles, and the basin and its stand.

en.L: and the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand.
en.B: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
en.R: the altar for burnt offerings and all the things used with it, and the bronze bowl and its stand.

decisions.choice: the altar of burnt offering ... the basin: the furnishings of the courtyard
decisions.reason: After the furnishings inside the tent (verses 26-27) come those in the courtyard: the bronze altar (27:1-8) and the basin (verse 18).

source.text: וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֣ אֹתָ֔ם וְהָי֖וּ קֹ֣דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֑ים כָּל־הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּהֶ֖ם יִקְדָּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will consecrate them, and they will be holiness of holinesses; every [thing] which touches them will be holy.

en.L: And you will consecrate them, and they will be most holy; whatever touches them will be holy.
en.B: In this way you are to consecrate them, and they will be most holy. Anything that touches them will become holy.
en.R: In this way you will set them apart for God, and they will be most holy. Anything that touches them will become holy too.

decisions.choice: consecrate: make holy, set apart for God
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to set something apart from ordinary use for God's service. The anointing is the means.

decisions.choice: whatever touches them will be holy: holiness passes to what touches them
alternatives: whatever touches them must be holy
decisions.reason: The verb may mean that whatever touches these things becomes holy and so belongs to God, or that only what is holy may touch them. The same phrase is used of the altar in 29:37 and of the offerings in Leviticus 6:18, 27.

decisions.choice: set them apart for God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "consecrate".

source.text: וְאֶת־אַהֲרֹ֥ן וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו תִּמְשָׁ֑ח וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם לְכַהֵ֥ן לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And Aaron and his sons you will anoint, and you will consecrate them to serve as priests to me.

en.L: And Aaron and his sons you will anoint, and you will consecrate them to serve as priests to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.
en.R: Anoint Aaron and his sons, and set them apart to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.

decisions.choice: anoint and consecrate Aaron and his sons: as in 28:41 and 29:7
decisions.reason: The priests are anointed with the same oil as the tent and its furnishings. The ceremony is described in 29:1-9 and carried out in Leviticus 8:12, 30.

source.text: וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר שֶׁ֠מֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹ֨דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֥ה זֶ֛ה לִ֖י לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to the sons of Israel you will speak, saying, an oil of anointing of holiness will be this to me throughout your generations.

en.L: And to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel you will speak, saying, 'This will be a holy anointing oil to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} throughout your generations.
en.B: Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'This is to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy anointing oil, generation after generation.
en.R: Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy anointing oil. It must be used only for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for all time to come.

decisions.choice: to me: belonging to God, for his use alone
decisions.reason: The oil is God's. Verses 32-33 spell out what that means: it may not be used for any other purpose.

decisions.choice: the words to Israel run to the end of verse 33
decisions.reason: Moses is to pass on to the people the rules about the oil. Verses 32-33 speak to "you" in the plural and seem to continue the message.

decisions.choice: It must be used only for me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "to me", following m1 and verses 32-33.

source.text: עַל־בְּשַׂ֤ר אָדָם֙ לֹ֣א יִיסָ֔ךְ וּבְמַ֨תְכֻּנְתּ֔וֹ לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ כָּמֹ֑הוּ קֹ֣דֶשׁ ה֔וּא קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] body of a person not it will be poured, and in its proportion not you must make like it; holy it [is], holy it will be to you.

en.L: On the flesh of a human it will not be poured, and by its formula you must not make [any] like it; it [is] holy; holy it will be to you.
en.B: It must not be poured on ordinary human flesh, and you must not make any oil like it by the same recipe. It is holy, and you are to treat it as holy.
en.R: Do not pour it on ordinary people. Do not use the same recipe to make any oil like it. It is holy, and you must treat it as holy.

decisions.choice: the body of a person: ordinary people, not the priests
decisions.reason: The oil was for the priests and the holy things. Pouring it on anyone else would treat a holy thing as common.

decisions.choice: its proportion: its recipe
decisions.reason: The word means a measured amount or proportion, the mix of spices given in verses 23-24.

decisions.choice: it is holy, holy it will be to you: you must treat it as holy
decisions.reason: The repetition presses the point: what is holy in itself must be treated as holy by the people.

decisions.choice: ordinary
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "ordinary" to show that the priests, who were anointed with it (verse 30), are not meant.

source.text: אִ֚ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִרְקַ֣ח כָּמֹ֔הוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִתֵּ֛ן מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַל־זָ֑ר וְנִכְרַ֖ת מֵעַמָּֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: A man who mixes like it and who puts of it on a stranger, then he will be cut off from his kinspeople.

en.L: Anyone who mixes [any] like it, or who puts [any] of it on an outsider, will be cut off from {{gender:their|his}} people.'"
en.B: Whoever blends any like it, or puts any of it on someone who is not a priest, is to be cut off from {{gender:their|his}} people.'"
en.R: Anyone who makes oil like it, or who puts it on someone who is not a priest, must be cut off from {{gender:their|his}} people.'"

decisions.choice: a stranger: an outsider to the priesthood
decisions.reason: The word means someone who does not belong. Here it is anyone who is not a priest, as in 29:33 and Numbers 16:40.

decisions.choice: cut off from his people: removed from the community
decisions.reason: The phrase means being removed from Israel, perhaps by death at God's hand or by being put out of the community. It is the same penalty as in 12:15, 19.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: Gender setting: the law applies to any person.

decisions.choice: someone who is not a priest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the "stranger" is, following m1. Literal says "outsider".

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֜ה קַח־לְךָ֣ סַמִּ֗ים נָטָ֤ף׀וּשְׁחֵ֨לֶת֙ וְחֶלְבְּנָ֔ה סַמִּ֖ים וּלְבֹנָ֣ה זַכָּ֑ה בַּ֥ד בְּבַ֖ד יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, take for yourself spices, stacte and onycha and galbanum, spices and frankincense pure; part for part it will be.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take for yourself spices, stacte and onycha and galbanum, spices and pure frankincense; part for part it will be.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take fragrant spices, stacte, onycha and galbanum, spices together with pure frankincense, an equal weight of each.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Get some sweet spices: stacte, onycha and galbanum. Add pure frankincense. Use the same amount of each.

decisions.choice: stacte: a fragrant gum, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: The word means "drops". It is probably a resin that drips from a tree, such as storax or a kind of myrrh, but the plant is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: onycha: a fragrant substance, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It is often taken to be the shell-like cover of a sea snail, which gives off a scent when burned, but it may be a plant resin.

decisions.choice: galbanum and frankincense, part for part: two resins in equal amounts
decisions.reason: Galbanum is a bitter-smelling gum from a plant of Persia; its identity is fairly certain. Frankincense is the white resin of a tree of Arabia and East Africa. "Part for part" means equal amounts of each spice.

decisions.choice: stacte, onycha, galbanum
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the traditional names of the uncertain spices rather than guess at modern ones; the footnotes give the possibilities.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֹתָהּ֙ קְטֹ֔רֶת רֹ֖קַח מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רוֹקֵ֑חַ מְמֻלָּ֖ח טָה֥וֹר קֹֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make it incense, an ointment, [the] work of a perfumer, salted, pure, holy.

en.L: And you will make it [into] incense, a blend, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure, holy.
en.B: Blend them into incense as a skilled perfumer would. It is to be seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
en.R: Mix them the way a skilled perfume maker would to make incense. Add salt to it. It must be pure and holy.

decisions.choice: salted: seasoned with salt
decisions.reason: Salt was added to every offering (Leviticus 2:13). The word may also mean "mixed" or "blended", but "salted" is its usual sense.

decisions.choice: pure, holy: unmixed with anything else, and set apart for God
decisions.reason: "Pure" means clean and unmixed; "holy" means it belongs to God alone (verse 37).

source.text: וְשָֽׁחַקְתָּ֣ מִמֶּנָּה֮ הָדֵק֒ וְנָתַתָּ֨ה מִמֶּ֜נָּה לִפְנֵ֤י הָעֵדֻת֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִוָּעֵ֥ד לְךָ֖ שָׁ֑מָּה קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים תִּהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will beat fine some of it, finely, and you will put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting where I will meet with you there; holiness of holinesses it will be to you.

en.L: And you will beat some of it very fine, and you will put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you; most holy it will be to you.
en.B: Pound some of it into fine powder and set some before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. You are to regard it as most holy.
en.R: Grind some of it into powder. Put some in front of the ark that holds the covenant tablets in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. You must treat this incense as most holy.

decisions.choice: before the testimony: in front of the ark that holds the tablets
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the covenant tablets in the ark (verse 6). The incense was placed in the holy place before the curtain, on the altar of incense, which stood in front of the ark.

decisions.choice: most holy: wholly God's
decisions.reason: The same doubled phrase as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the testimony", as in verse 6.

source.text: וְהַקְּטֹ֨רֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה בְּמַ֨תְכֻּנְתָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶ֑ם קֹ֛דֶשׁ תִּהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the incense which you will make, in its proportion not you must make for yourselves; holy it will be to you, to Yahweh.

en.L: And the incense that you will make, by its formula you must not make [any] for yourselves; it will be holy to you, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: As for the incense you are to make, you must never make any by the same recipe for yourselves. You are to count it holy, belonging to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Do not use this recipe to make incense for yourselves. It is holy. It belongs only to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: its proportion: its recipe
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, the word means the measured mix of spices.

decisions.choice: holy to Yahweh: reserved for God alone
decisions.reason: The incense, like the anointing oil, may not be used for any ordinary purpose because it belongs to the LORD.

source.text: אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה כָמ֖וֹהָ לְהָרִ֣יחַ בָּ֑הּ וְנִכְרַ֖ת מֵעַמָּֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: A man who makes like it to smell it, then he will be cut off from his kinspeople.

en.L: Anyone who makes [any] like it to smell it will be cut off from {{gender:their|his}} people."
en.B: Whoever makes any like it for the pleasure of its scent is to be cut off from {{gender:their|his}} people."
en.R: Anyone who makes incense like it just to enjoy its smell must be cut off from {{gender:their|his}} people."

decisions.choice: to smell it: to enjoy it as a perfume
decisions.reason: The verb means to smell or enjoy a scent. The incense may not be made for private pleasure.

decisions.choice: cut off from his people: removed from the community
decisions.reason: As in verse 33.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: Gender setting: the law applies to any person.
